Flag for IDT/prescriber review whether dual therapy is intended and whether the indication for clopidogrel is still current; check for bleeding signs (melena, hematuria, bruising, epistaxis), and hemoglobin trend given the anemia diagnosis.

Renal function trend: pull creatinine/eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio for the window and prior review, given diabetic kidney disease, microalbuminuria, proteinuria, and CKD staging; confirm it is consistent with the apixaban dosing and any renal-related medication decisions.

Glycemic status: review HbA1c and glucose values since last review given prediabetes on the problem list alongside a diabetes-related kidney diagnosis and proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes; reconcile whether the diabetes label is current and whether any glucose-lowering therapy is listed (none appears on the active list).

Blood pressure trend for the window (essential hypertension) and any orthostatic readings, since a new anticoagulant and fall risk both depend on it; note antihypertensive status, which is not on the active list and needs reconciliation.
Weight and BMI trend (BMI 30+ / obesity and metabolic syndrome), including any unintended weight change; check that recorded weight is available for anticoagulant dosing.
Sleep apnea follow-up: confirm CPAP or other OSA treatment use and adherence, sleep-related symptoms, and any recent sleep study or equipment issues.

Atrial fibrillation management: check rate or rhythm control status, symptoms (palpitations, dyspnea, dizziness, syncope), recent ECG or cardiology follow-up, and stroke/bleeding risk discussion documented for the IDT.

Falls, ED visits, and hospital admissions since 2026-09-01: review incident reports, ED and admission records, and whether any event followed the apixaban start (2026-09-07). Also check the anemia workup status and colon/rectal polyp surveillance (recurrent rectal polyp, 2018) for any GI bleeding history or overdue colonoscopy, since both bear on anticoagulation safety.
